en: Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
*Pajjamadhu*:
Ānanda, the King, the Great Lord of Sacrifice beginning with the Jewels.
May those who delight in the lotus-like feet of the Buddha,
whose limbs are ever-awakened, drink this honey of verses composed by the Elder Āli, who is dear to the Buddha and fond of the Buddha’s profound qualities.
Flowing down from the orb of his moon-like ūrṇā-hair,
like a stream of nectar-drops from the petals of the toes of his lotus feet,
the Teacher’s row of nails seemed to distinguish the excellence of the people.
May the Teacher, whose mind is pure and blissful, who has conquered the enemy Māra,
and who has subdued the quarters with his cool, white, and radiant feet,
be satisfied by this offering of food. May he grant us happiness.
That which conquers all the splendor of a row of lakes with its beauty,
that very hand— with its beautiful fingers victorious in battle—
is like a golden-colored, delicate-skinned, and gentle tortoise.
May the feet of the Victor— whose backs shine with a curvature like that of a tortoise shell,
and whose long soles are well-set and very tender—
grant a foothold for people.
A marvel! Those who, as if intoxicated,
move with their heads bowed toward the lotuses by their own splendor, and those [lotuses] whose pollen,
as if kissed by passion, cling to their heads— [such is the union of the two].
May those dustless feet of the Sage bestow prosperity—
feet that were fashioned here as if by a skilled craftsman to proclaim the auspicious nature of the Lord to the world at the time of his departure.
May his pair of feet accomplish the auspicious marks of a hundredfold prosperity for the journey;
may they be honored at the entrance to the city of Varanasi.
May those who possess the auspicious marks that bestow victory and fortune— those who are ever ready,
as if established for the sake of blessing—
turn toward the feet of the Victor for the sake of victorious auspiciousness.
Having overcome all [opponents] through his authoritative citations,
he who beholds the entire world as if it were a mere signpost— even though he possesses the supreme sovereignty over the three worlds whose heads are bowed at his feet—
May they bring prosperity to the world as the causes of victory and auspiciousness. Wherein the world is well-arranged,
he stands ready, as it were, to manifest his state as the sole refuge for the three worlds.
May those two feet, possessing a luster like a mirror reflecting the entire world,
be for the sake of the well-behaved and the virtuous people,
so that they may thoroughly attain supramundane glory.
May those two feet of his— whose thousand rays,
like a thousand spokes, naves, hubs, and rims,
protect all beings as if they were twice as dear— manifest their universal sovereignty to the world.
Wherein the two kinds of wheels, as if manifesting, shine forth—
the wheels of the Dhamma and the wheels of sovereignty over all worlds—
of the Well-Seer, who resembles a wheel-turning monarch.
May these today be a refuge and a protection for people.
May the Śrīvatsa mark bestow prosperity upon beings,
and may the Svastika attend to the well-being of individuals.
May he who follows the joy of people experience that very joy;
may he who is an ornament for the feet adorn the heads [of others];
may he who approaches the auspicious seat attain the truly auspicious throne.
May the people follow after increasing prosperity;
may the full water-pot emulate the excellence of its form;
and may the protective vessel constantly protect the people from the lower realms.
May it remove the white sunshade from the heat of evil;
may the sword always sever the hosts of enemies that are misfortune;
and may the fan with its hundred ribs dispel the burning heat of affliction.
It terrifies the flies of the wicked mind and the hands of the peacock of pride;
it draws in the eyes of people who have fallen into the mire of negligence;
may that goad, which wards off all states of existence, protect us.
May the clarity of mind attain the characteristics of a palace,
like the abode of the glorious splendor of his lotus feet;
may it be a noble vessel of merit for those who partake of his presence.
May he who rightly gives with a bowl of merit resting upon his feet,
subdue that tethering rope which binds people to his feet—
a rope that should instead tame the stainless minds of the multitude.
May his feet, adorned with the jewels of the uṇhīsa-tuft and lotuses,
and which cause those who serve him to flourish,
be honored by those who have approached him as their guide— feet that are priceless.
The ocean bestowed the seven treasures of the factors of enlightenment.
With its lofty and steady waves, it constantly bore the glory of his feet, as if serving him out of devotion.
Here too, he was engaged in surpassing the realm of Sakka;
with his own splendor, he surpassed Mount Meru,
the summit of the world-system, on every side.
The entire assembly of kings, free from all calamities, remained united;
even the many four great islands and two thousand small ones sustained themselves,
preventing people from falling into states of misery.
May the sun awaken all beings as it awakens the day-lotuses;
may the moon gladden the night-lotuses in the lakes of their minds;
and may the entire host of stars bring forth auspiciousness.
The Wheel and the Banner for victory over enemies, the banner of victory;
by which one might bring here the Cakravartin,
who is beautiful with his retinue, gracefully following the wheels.
The world-ruling monarch who follows the wheel and turns the wheel has come to honor that pair of feet which turn all beings for the welfare of the people;
indeed, he has come while seated upon the diamond throne.
May this conch shell, known as Mahāvijayuttara,
which has been cast away by the mind like one that has entered beneath the foot out of fear of Māra,
bring you peace when placed at your feet.
O people, may you possess a pair of golden fish for the enjoyment of peaceful food,
and may you have many desired requisites;
[may you be freed] from those with defiled minds, like the one seized by the crocodile.
May they plunge into the lake of your lotus feet;
may they cast off the impurities of the minds of beings, who are like rivers,
and may they extinguish the burning heat of the afflictions of those beings.
May these seven [treatises] provide protection for people;
may they become banners for the production of worldly renown.
May they be beneficial in the journey toward the state of a saint (pāṭaṅki).
May that foot-fan, which has abandoned those who were once consumed by fever,
and which is raised like a great festival for the eyes of the world,
serve as a supreme auspicious archway.
O Lord of Beasts, in whom fear has entered and is firmly burnt away,
who are bowed down by generosity as if oppressed by the rending of his own crest;
[therein dwell] Nālāgiri, the noble elephant, and Girimekhala.
May the King of Golden Feet, the Lord of Tigers, the destroyer of the wicked,
utterly annihilate all those who do not give in this age of strife,
just as one slays a bellowing cow by following the lion’s stride.
May the Lord of Horses, Vālāha, not allow [anyone] to approach,
but let him lead the people to the presence of the Sage.
May the rut flowing from the temples of the Chaddanta elephant bring grace.
Displaying his trunk as motionless as a mountain, the lordly elephant,
standing on his hind legs, now terrifies the people;
may he strike terror into the hearts of those who mock the truth of the virtuous.
May the king of elephants, who observes the Uposatha with all his limbs,
attain the auspicious sovereignty over all four continents;
may fame indeed be appointed as his attendant.
One should practice the black art of *kela-sāselapaṭimā*.
Like a goose bound by a net at the command of its master,
one should be like a foot-goose (*pādahaṃsa*) that has entered the village.
Like one who has conquered the path of speech through the cessation of sound,
may he cause all people to abandon the wandering through existence;
having left behind the celestial lake and the entire world of worldly attachments.
Having plunged his feet into the lovely lake of the ocean,
the noble elephant Erāvaṇa seemed as swift as one carrying a person who has mounted him in his mind toward the city of Indra.
Having abandoned the forest of Sakambhana for the sake of serving the feet [of the Buddha],
do not come here, O delightful one, but remain dependent on this [place];
having protected the waves of the shore established at my head, [you shall attain your goal].
The Naga king Vāsuki, having taken hold of his own body,
displayed the playful beauty of his golden crests for the Lord,
like a peacock king perched upon a foot.
With the sound of that teaching of the Dhamma, he destroyed the hunter—
just as one destroys the world’s serpent of evil— without remainder;
[he rescued] those people with their wealth who had fallen into the ocean of saṃsāra.
Just as a wise and well-oared ship reaches the excellent port of Nirvana from the beautiful harbor of Bharukaccha,
so too did the ship of the four-faced Kālaka reach the city of Netamapada.
Just as the elephant of Himavat was devoted to the Sage who was ripening the knowledge of perfect enlightenment for the sake of concentration, so too,
O people, do you resort to the foothills of Himavat with a devoted mind.
May this serve as the cause for maturing the knowledge of perfect enlightenment.
Like a bird confined within a cage of empty reeds by the cry of the Sage who has utterly conquered [the defilements], [I am bound].
Thus, the karavīka bird confined within the cage of his feet abandoned all unpleasant speech toward you;
so too did the cakravāka, the makara, the krauñca, and the jīvaṃjīvaka.
May beings always find delight in those footprints,
just as a multitude of living creatures in a lake that has been enjoyed by Vessantara,
while they tread upon his lotus-like feet.

Then the Kinnara and the Kinnarī, as if indicating the state of that being who had attained the gait of the moon-like Kinnara— his awakening and his condition together with his wife— spoke these words.
May they attain the path of harmony. May the bull,
the leader of the herd, bearing the foremost burden,
produce milk for his calf with joyful flow.
May the six heavens of sensual pleasure rejoice in their eternal splendor;
may the sixteen elements, the abodes of the meditator, be maintained here.
Having heard the melodious and pleasing voice of the Conqueror, like that of a cuckoo—
Though they are adversaries, they are free from fear of one another;
having abandoned their own course like a path, they stand in the form of footprints—
may they destroy the state of non-going for all people who dwell in existence.
The golden lute and its pair of strings, like the wealth of Indra,
and the fresh water-lily buds, like the beauty of a woman—
these were always kept ready and set out before him as he stood there, O Sage.
May his two shanks, which resemble a pair of mirrors for the playful movements of the eyes of the people, and his mass of hair,
which mocks the ornamentation of earrings, be for the welfare of all.
His two knees, resembling the bubbles on the playful ocean,
serve to adorn the three worlds;
they are like a pair of excellent tusks bestowed as a gift.
May those who possess the trunk-like arms of an elephant, whose form is filled with merit,
who are like the playful ocean, the glory, and the golden plantain tree in sport,
bestow upon people the perfection of all virtues.
O Sage, your two wheels are the mind and the heart-steed, with the feet of consciousness joined to the axle of the shanks;
this glorious chariot, borne by wisdom, has been mounted by you with the mind.
May she swiftly lead the three worlds to the city of peace.
On the banks of the beautiful and famous lake,
the line of body hair is like a million water-channels flowing with water.
May the navel of the goddess Śrī, who sports in that deep lake,
dispel the heat and impurity of calamity for those who seek refuge in her.
The navel of the ocean of forms, stirred by the radiance of her beauty—
The entire world has been whirled around, turned over,
and submerged; having drunk the flood of the waters of beauty,
may it attain a state of swoon from the bliss of the supramundane and other such states.
Having filled the deep lake of his heart,
which is like a flowing stream of the waters of compassion,
with its golden hair-furrows as shimmering vines and its beautiful navel as a lovely basin;
O Sage, may these [verses] of yours—possessing beautiful *sāri* fruits, curved tips, and fine hair;
arranged in rows with proper division; endowed with glory;
and ready for the play of poetic beauty—swiftly yield the fruit of peace for those who partake in them.
For the sake of the game of dice that is the happiness of heaven and liberation,
those intoxicated with pleasure engage in the game of dice that is the happiness of the three worlds.
Plunging into the deep lake of the mind, they seek its depths.
O Lord, may your arms, like branches of the celestial tree, bestow upon us all limbs— the bridegroom’s hands joined with the bride’s—
and grant the fruit of auspiciousness. May they embrace you.
It shone with the beauty of its tips and petals adorned with dewdrops,
possessing the grace of two hanging red lotuses;
it was as red as if stained by the blood from the severed head of an enemy of evil.
Your red hands have become auspicious upon the earth. Your bodily splendor,
your conduct, and the grace of your gait are such that your back appears like a bridge of white clay upon the head of the world.
Thus, for the purpose of crossing over the ocean of existence, it is like a bridge,
resembling a great golden causeway;
it is the delightful sounding of the drum of the teaching of the True Dharma.
May the beautiful golden neck-ornaments and the *mutiṅga* and *bherī* drums [of the celestial musicians] become a source of prosperity for you as people travel to visit the city of Śiva.
The lotus-face of the one dwelling in Lakhī, intoxicated with joy,
draws in the bees that are the eyes of the people,
while distilling the nectar of the fragrance of his virtuous conduct.
Let the people in the assembly be delighted by that nectar-like speech.
The wheels of his chariot have ascended to the heights of fortune,
and the playfulness of his cheeks rivals the king of beasts.
Adorning the two cheeks of the people like a pair of earrings with rounded tips,
they shone like two coral creepers from the ocean of loveliness.
O Goddess, let your two red lips— beautiful as the sprouts of the coral tree,
possessing the splendor of jasmine and the nectar of a blooming lotus— subdue the sins of mankind.
The wool, the bird, the head, the nose, the pit,
the virtuous one, the letter *la*, together with the lip, coral, and the ship—
these have come upon the ocean of the limbs of you, O Protector of beings.
O Lord, this is the method for crossing the ocean of existence:
the row of your beautiful teeth, adorned with playful grace,
is like a cluster of filaments within the heart of a blooming lotus.
Speech is like a bride adorned with a garland of jasmine;
one should act so as to delight the mind of that person.
It possesses the beauty of a dark-red stone slab from which the stream of the True Dhamma flows.
May your tongue, speech, dance, wife, voice, theater,
and spirits become the most excellent true Dhamma, the boat for crossing over, which you hold dear,
for the purpose of crossing over the ocean of saṃsāra.
Your tusks are like ivory pillars draped in saffron-colored robes as you exert yourself in striving;
your tongue is crimson-red, resting in the temple of your mouth upon your couch;
and your wife, Liberation, lies beside you until the final release from existence.
May those who desire to hear [this] create a gathering that is free from impurity.
Her eyebrows are like two beautiful, fresh leaves, lovely with their fine tips;
they are dark-blue petals, shimmering with playful movement.
May the beautiful plantain tree with its lovely trunk and face of fresh sprouts long bring auspiciousness to you, O people! May she,
who reclines upon the surface of the stone slab of the young elephant’s temple, [grant you blessings].
O you who possess a pair of peacock feathers like two creeping vines upon the earth,
may your pair of eyes— resplendent with the beauty of five-colored,
radiant plumage— wipe away the dust of evil from my mind.
A row of bees has settled within the blue lotuses,
like a line of trees upon the expanse of a lake of five-colored lotuses;
it is as if it were a veil obscuring the beauty of your lotus-like eyes.
May the rows of lotus filaments, surpassing the temple of her head,
shine with the luster of two stalks of white lotus fibers—
golden like the beaks of swans and resembling the petals of a circular lotus in her eyes.
Just as the two ears perceive the two sounds of a swing, so too, O King,
does the multitude today experience this through the movement of their intellects.
Like Bhūridatta lying upon the summit of an anthill, [he remains unmoved].
O Sage, established above the nose, may your high and low folds of skin,
which move with the graceful undulation of a serpent-king’s coils,
grant wealth to those people who grasp them as if they were you.
In the conquest of the beauty of the sense-pleasures of form, the world’s beauty is but a mere trifle;
even the most exquisite and lovely forms are like fetters bound upon the thighs of perfected beings,
shimmering with the hue of sapphire as they flutter in the wind.
Let your enemies remain subdued for your victory.
Your hips are set upon elevated stones, and your thighs,
calves, and roundness of the buttocks are firmly established.
The glory of the lotus-face, with its radiance streaming from the head;
the golden parasol upon the forehead adorned with a blue silk band;
and the eyes, which are like the lotus-pool, casting glances like arrows.
May the splendor of your head, with its crest-jewel set upon a polished base,
and the mass of perfected medicinal herbs and collyrium,
serve to destroy the eye-disease of the people.
With the body as the archway, the pair of arms as the gateway, the neck as the middle,
and the head-dress as the treasure-chamber, falsehood was completely covered;
lovely blue lotuses were placed there with due arrangement.
May his hair be for the blessing of the three worlds. Resting upon the golden throne,
it resembles a sapphire bowl set with a network of radiant light,
evoking the memory of the Sage.
May a golden garland, like the glory of form adorning a head,
create for you an auspicious banner-garland;
may the radiance of your two arms be like that of a golden peacock.
May the golden mountain, its lofty peaks shrouded by clouds,
with its expansive moon-like circular eyes at sunrise,
grant splendor like the wondrous display of a mechanical bow.
From the moment you made that aspiration, your pure giving and virtue,
renunciation, wisdom, energy, patience, commitment to truth,
loving-kindness, and equanimity— these ten have indeed been fulfilled.
May the virtues of the perfections fulfill the needs of all people.
Having reached ever-higher stages through the seeds of aspiration,
may they grow by the watering of the water of compassion within the soil of the mind.
May the creeper of your perfections, guarded by the fence of mindfulness that yields the fruit of omniscient knowledge, blossom forth for you.
May it be seen from the very first day of the waxing moon until the full moon of enlightenment.
Increasing gradually during the bright fortnight of the period of accumulation, may you—
like the moon whose rays are the immeasurable virtues of the perfections—
awaken all the jasmine and water lilies of every limb.
Through giving, you obtained the fruit of auspiciousness in your final existence;
you increased this succession of gifts and the abundance of their fruits through your aspiration, just as it was.
May they indeed attain successively higher fruits.
From the very beginning of their undertaking until the highest path,
may their pure water of virtue have its turbid mud stirred up and cleared away.
Endowed with loving-kindness, compassion, sweetness,
and coolness, may you alone purify these beings who are dependent on existence.
From the very moment of your renunciation until the final limit, [may this be so].
Having departed from that very existence with a complete household,
you have even gone forth from every kind of birth;
thus, indeed, may people depart from the suffering of existence.
Firmly fixed on the palm of the hand, the arrow was held steady for a long time;
the bowstring was bound with care, and mindfulness was applied to the handle.
Having become disillusioned with worldly things, he took as his target the peace established by the marks of excellence.
May the person who has cast [the hook] pierce the three [realms];
you, O Lord, are like a father to people, having for long cast the four perfections as a hook into the ocean of the waters here, like a fisherman casting his line into the sea.
Just as you have attained the fruit of perfected valor,
so may people likewise enjoy the fruit of their own diligence.
May beings long endure well-refined amidst the fires of the world beyond.
Patience is like gold that has been well-fashioned;
you have endured all insults, even those that were unbearable.
May all people likewise attain peace through patience.
For a period of time numbering four plus a hundred thousand aeons,
those whose speech was thoroughly permeated by truth—
by means of that speech touched by truth, they brought people together.
May the people thus become pure in speech.
With the Dharma you have received as your foundation, may they be firm and well-established;
may your diamond-like thunderbolt of the perfections of fortitude be great.
Just as no one at all can divide the unbreakable ocean,
so too should people be resolute in wholesome qualities. You,
whose mind of loving-kindness has long been cultivated toward all beings—
O Fire, extinguish anger completely;
bring welfare to both the supramundane and the mundane.
May you thus bring welfare to the people among mankind.
O you who are free from change through long-cultivated mental composure,
you perceive the hostility of those who have done you harm as a benefit;
O you who remain unshaken amidst gains, honors, and various forms of praise.
May people thus be free from attachment and aversion.
Having perfected the causes for prosperity, may they dwell in the Tuṣita heaven,
a celestial palace endowed with ninefold virtues and a place of supreme bliss.
May you, who have reached the supreme state,
ascend to the celestial palace— the path of fearlessness and bliss—
in this triple world. Just as you have perfectly awakened to the solitary peace, so too [may others attain it].
May you be one perfected in true knowledge and conduct, a Sugata;
may you be a knower of the world, a charioteer of men to be tamed,
a Teacher, an Awakened One, and likewise a Blessed One for all beings.
The people have deposited their own hearts within you,
who possess the jewel of a beautiful complexion and a noble birth, like a treasure hidden in the earth;
for they dwell in a home where the fires of suffering, thieves, and floods have afflicted their lives.
May she have happiness throughout her life.
Your speech is variegated, with excellent threads woven through its limbs;
released from your throat, it is a garland of great jewels of virtue.
Having completely abandoned his former complexion and stature, may this Lord become a source of glory for the people, a blessing for their prosperity. May this work,
which contains excellent verses and is adorned with beautiful annotations, [be completed].
May people who perceive this field as a fertile plot— those who have planted the hair-like stalks of virtue, which are the drinking pools for the flowing water of merit—
obtain the fruit of the harvest of wholesome sprouts.
During the season of the heat of suffering, beginning with the states of woe,
the minds of all beings in the world were scorched like kadamba flowers;
yet by the touch of the cloud of his complexion, they sprouted with the buds of laughter.
May the creeper of your intellect flourish,
established equally in the stage of the cause and the stage of the fruit,
perfected by bringing benefit to all beings everywhere.
May there be well-being for all beings through the accomplishment of the wondrous purpose of your conduct,
O you whose power transcends the path of thought and whose majesty is infinite! When,
at the time of giving, you leaped over the pit of glowing coals—
And the lotuses that conceal the soles of your feet—
may those lotuses, at the very moment they rise up from your feet,
bestow auspicious honey upon us.
By truth, O Lord of Fishes, you have caused a stream of rain to fall;
by compassion for living beings, a stream of rain has fallen from you.
Just as it was for people in the summer heat, so have they been cooled.
May the rain of the Dhamma extinguish the fever of the defilements.
Just as the elephant king Chaddanta, having forgiven the hunter’s offense,
cut off his own two excellent tusks and placed them in the hunter’s hand;
Your tooth relic, established for the welfare of the world,
may it most excellently lead people swiftly to the city of peace.
That [relic] was placed within the stupa of the ascetic named Temiya.
Strewn with pearls and scattered with gold, these relics—
kinsmen to the drops of water fallen from the cloud of your compassion—
may they allay the fever of suffering in living beings.
Like a pair of sandals made of grass given by Rāma for the sake of the kingdom's welfare while he was absent,
these have been enjoyed by you for a long time while I remained away and did not come before you.
"May the relics that have been obtained remain for the welfare of the world"—
this was declared by the King, observing the people,
like one who knows the Dhamma as clearly as sixty thousand autumn moons.
Having observed what is to be accepted and what is to be abandoned,
may the Dhamma proclaimed by you endure for a long time for the welfare of the people,
bringing about the attainment of benefit through the crushing of the enemy, Māra.
O noble one, may you, the great and victorious King Bodhi,
having destroyed all obstacles for the sake of the welfare of people— both in the heavenly realms and the state beyond the world—
remain here well-prepared and steadfast.
In this cluster of virtues worthy of veneration and fragrant with joy,
the creeper of your conduct has blossomed with fruitful branches;
it delights the honey-bees of those whose minds are scattered, nourishing them with its nectar.
May the one honored on earth proceed at our heads.
O you who are called "Knowledge," dwelling within the circle of mountains of the Fully Enlightened One,
you who do not waver from your state, you who go by the three paths and abide in the ocean.
The teachings, like clear waters, flow according to the ear;
they purify, and here they cause the harvest of requisites to ripen.
One who grasps the wind of exertion, seated at the well of wisdom, [draws forth the water].
May the boat of mindfulness, equipped with the oars of faith,
carry me across the ocean of existence to the shore of the supreme city,
reaching the excellent harbor filled with the wealth of liberation.
The seven factors of enlightenment are the mine of jewels, the Dhamma-aggregate;
the ocean of the Dispensation has a depth of accumulated waters.
It is encircled by the infinite body of virtue and churned by the churning-stick of wisdom.
Having churned the ocean of the Dhamma,
it is indeed considered by the wise that by following that very method taught therein,
one obtains and experiences that deathless state which destroys all barrenness and faults.

May the Dhamma-ray issued forth from the sun of the King of the True Dhamma transform this world— which is overwhelmed by absolute disease, decay, and death— into that which is immortal, ageless, and free from illness.
May the lotus-pond of the Dispensation, born from the waters of the Sāsana—
its petals the ascetic practices (dhutaṅga), its filaments the vows (saṃvara), its multitude of blossoms the Saṅgha, and its honey the meditative concentration (samādhi)— be seen by you.
Ānanda, the king who possesses great power over jewels and other riches,
whose limbs are served by women who are ever-awake and fond of lotuses,
[was surpassed] by Buddhapiya, who is deeply devoted to the virtues of the Buddha.
May they drink the honeyed verses composed by Therāli.
Thus, through the power of describing his various virtues, may my mindfulness toward him be for my benefit,
and may my loving-kindness toward all beings proceed here as it does through the recollection of the Buddha.
Thus, O venerable ones, may you speak ever more excellently for my sake regarding enlightenment,
as well as regarding union with wealth, peace, and virtuous friends.
